summary: Proof that a keyed BINARY (streaming) mutation keeps the keep-alive-free HTTP/1 transport (Codex gocli1219-r2 P3): TestKeyedStreamingMutationClientHasKeepAlivesOffAndIsHTTP1 pins the policy attemptHTTPClient hands the streaming read (keyed: DisableKeepAlives, HTTP/1 only; unkeyed: the HTTP/1-only mutation transport; wrapper: refused, no client); TestKeyedStreamingMutationDroppedAfterAWarmCallIsSentOnceOnAFreshConnection shows end to end that a keyed streaming /drop after a warm keyed call is one hit on a fresh connection.
reason: The r2 streaming test asserted HTTP/1.1 only, which the ordinary keep-alive mutation transport also satisfies.
validated_outcome: The policy test fails with keep-alives left on in the keyed transport and fails when the streaming branch wraps the shared client; StreamingHTTPClient clones the transport per call, so the warm/drop test alone cannot tell a pooled policy apart (noted in the test).
